title: Picking up the partial sums of the Möbius function problem with probabilistic number theory
summary: We revisit several hybrid multiplicative-to-additive type functions from a recent preprint article. These functions, $g(n)$ with Dirichlet generating function (DGF) $ζ(s)^{-1} (1+P(s))^{-1}$ for $\Re(s) > 1$ where $P(s) = \sum_p p^{-s}$ is the prime zeta function, $|g(n)| = λ(n) g(n)$ with DGF $ζ(2s)^{-1}(1-P(s))^{-1}$, and $C_Ω(n)$ with DGF $(1-P(s))^{-1}$. Each of these function variants are defined in terms of the additive (respectively, strongly additive) functions $ω(n)$ and $Ω(n)$.
